newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - TIM reports H1 profits 48 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - TIM reports H1 profits 48 pct higher.

text.p: Europe's largest mobile phone group Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) on Friday reported a 48 percent jump in profits as the Italian group continued to benefit from one of Europe's fastest growing mobile market.

The company reported a pretax profit of 955 billion lire ($627 million) in the first half of 1996, a 48 percent rise on its profits made in the last 5-1/2 months of 1995, while sales were up nearly 20 percent at 3.355 trillion lire.

The comparison was made with the last 5-1/2 months of 1995 since TIM was only spun off from state-controlled telecom holding group STET in mid-July 1995, with STET now holding around 62 percent of TIM shares.
TIM said that its number of clients rose by 16.2 percent in the first half of 1996 to 4.49 million, confirming the group as the fastest growing mobile phone group in Europe.

The group's total number of subscribers up to September 18 rose to 4.77 million, with its analogue network system subcribers totalling 3.81 million, while its newer GSM digital subscriber numbers rose to 971,501.
The Rome-based group said it had gained 624,000 new subscribers in the first half of 1996, of which some 305,000 were for its GSM digital phones.

Analysts highlighted that revenue growth of nearly 20 percent was above subscriber growth of 16 percent in the first half, indicating that usage per subscriber was on the increase and there was little sign of margin erosion.

"There is no doubt that this market is certainly big enough for two successful players," said industry analyst Evan Miller at investment bank CS First Boston in London. TIM's only other competitor in Italy, Omnitel, gained 500,000 GSM subcribers by the end of August since it launched its GSM service in December 1995. The Omnitel consortium, owned 41.3 percent by Olivetti and including U.S. groups AirTouch and Bell Atlantic, has been a strong competitor to TIM this year.

Italy is one of the Europe's fastest growing mobile phone markets where around 8.4 percent of the population has a mobile phone, up from 6.7 percent at the start of the year, but this level is below double-digit figures in Britain and over 20 percent levels in some Scandinavian countries.
TIM said its network now reached 62 percent of Italian territory and some 93 percent of the population.

The group said it had expanded in Latin America, Europe and Asia in the first half, and had earmarked 23 percent of its cash flow to invest in 12 percent of STET International -- the joint venture between STET and fixed-line operator Telecom Italia -- and 35 percent in Iridium Italia SpA.
At 1345 GMT, TIM shares were up 1.64 percent at 3,040 lire in a slightly firmer Milan stock market. ($1= 1,524 lire)
